verdict.rationale: Superset documents its own repo-onboarding flow: you add a repo from a local folder, or clone one through a dialog that lists the GitHub repositories available to the host's GitHub CLI login. Agents then work on that repo in isolated worktrees. Repo access still relies on an existing external GitHub CLI login rather than a first-party one-click install or authorization flow, and the 'no complex setup' claim is not independently corroborated. Missing for 10: a documented one-click install/authorization (e.g., GitHub App install), repo access that doesn't depend on an external gh CLI login, and hands-on evidence that setup is effortless.

support.subject: As a developer, I can grant an agent access to my repositories with a one-click install, without complex setup

citations.quote: Add your repo from a local folder or clone a remote repository. In the clone dialog, search the GitHub repositories available to the selected host's GitHub CLI login
Each agent gets an isolated Git worktree and its own branch.
